To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the T-violating asymmetries for neutrino oscillations in matter are (i) clean in a wide region of the (E,L) plane and (ii) can be measured in the clean region with a precision that can be comparable to or larger than the one obtained in the vacuum.

the genuine T-violation between v(alpha) and v(beta), and the matter-contamination of this T-violation, are both negligible in realistic neutrino experiments provided that the neutrino beam energies are sufficiently high.
the T-violating asymmetries in neutrino and antineutrino oscillations in matter are not contaminated by the matter effects and can be measured to an excellent accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new method for measuring T violation in neutrinos.
the possibility that the T-violating asymmetries in neutrino oscillation experiments are contaminated by the matter effects.
the study of the effects of matter in neutrino oscillation processes, in particular in the context of T-violation in neutrino oscillating beams.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the T-violating asymmetries between (v) over right arrow (alpha) ->(v) over right bar (beta) and (v(beta) -> (v(alpha)) over right arrow are clean in the presence of terrestrial matter effects for a realistic medium-or long baseline neutrino experiment provided the neutrino energy and baseline length satisfy the condition 1 x 10(-7)(L/km)(2)(E/GeV) v(alpha) and v(beta).
the clean T-violating asymmetries between v(beta) -> (v)(alpha) and (v)(alpha)(-> v)(beta) oscillations are measurable for a realistic medium-or long- baseline neutrino experiment.
clean T violation is not possible at a neutrino factory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the clean T violation is a realistic observable for neutrino experiments.
, if a realistic long-baseline neutrinos experiment is planned, it is necessary and important to choose the neutrino beam parameters E and L to avoid the matter contamination.

the clean T-violating asymmetries in (v) over (bar)(alpha) -> (bar) v(beta) oscillations can be observed with high confidence in realistic neutrino experiments, provided that the condition 10(7) (L/ km)(2) (E/GeV) is fulfilled.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a realistic experiment can be designed in such a way that the T-violating asymmetries in neutrino and antineutrino channels can be measured with an accuracy of a few percent.
a long-baseline neutrinos experiment with an energy of 10-100 GeV can be a powerful probe of CP violation in the lepton sector.
a realistic long-baseline experiment is able to probe the T violation in neutrinos with a precision that is not contaminated by the matter effect. (C) 2017 The Authors. Published
